title: SkillOpt: Self-Evolving Agent Skills with Zero Inference Overhead
story_key: story|title:skillopt self evolving agent skills with zero inference overhead
content_excerpt: SkillOpt is a text-space optimizer that trains reusable natural-language skills for frozen LLM agents through trajectory-driven edits, validation-gated updates, and deployable best_skill.md artifacts. Train agent skills like you train neural networks — with epochs, (mini-)batchsize, learning rates, and validation gates — but without touching model weights. 📖 For installation, data preparation, training/eval commands, configuration, and framework internals, start with the versioned SkillOpt documentation . A concise rendered overview is available in the Documentation & Reproduction Guide , and longer-form engineering analysis appears on the Technical Blog . We also maintain a Changelog for released and unreleased changes. Modern agent skills are usually hand-crafted, generated one-shot by a strong LLM, or evolved through loosely controlled self-revision — none of which behaves like a deep-learning optimizer for the skill itself, and none of which reliably improves over its starting point under feedback. SkillOpt treats the skill document as the trainable state of a frozen agent , and trains it with the discipline that makes weight-space optimization reproducible. A separate optimizer model turns scored rollouts into bounded add / delete / replace edits on a single skill document; in the default paper-style path, a candidate edit is accepted only when it strictly improves a held-out validation score. A textual learning-rate budget, a rejected-edit buffer, and an epoch-wise slow / meta update make skill training stable while adding zero inference-time model calls at deployment. The deployed artifact is a compact best_skill.md (typically 300–2,000 tokens) that runs against the unchanged target model. Across six benchmarks, seven target models, and three execution harnesses (direct chat, Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI), SkillOpt is best or tied-best on all 52 evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cells and on GPT-5.5 lifts the average no-skill accuracy by +23.5 points in direct chat, +24.8 inside the Codex agentic loop, and +19.1 inside Claude Code . Optimized skill artifacts transfer across model scales, between Codex and Claude Code harnesses, and to nearby benchmarks without further optimization. For the full method, ablations, and per-cell results see the paper ; for a visual walkthrough of the loop see the project page ; for deeper API / backend / benchmark docs see docs/ . title: Towards Verifiable LLM Infra: Agent-Driven Proof of Agent-Implemented Inference
story_key: story|title:towards verifiable llm infra agent driven proof of agent implemented inference
content_excerpt: Coding agents are getting remarkably good at writing LLM infrastructure, from GPU kernels and schedulers to custom serving engines. Suppose an AI agent is strong enough to build a fast inference engine from scratch; in this second half of the problem, the bottleneck shifts from capability to verification : how do we know the engine it wrote is actually correct? Passing latency and throughput benchmarks still leaves rare concurrency bugs hidden. As a single engineer begins orchestrating 100, 1,000, or even 10,000 coding agents in parallel, human code review hits a hard cognitive wall. Having agents review other agents does not solve this either; as pstack author Lauren Tan noted , adversarial reviews are mostly a waste of tokens, and it is far better to spend those tokens on empirical and formal verification. In this post, we introduce vstack , a 5-stage formal verification workflow for coding agents, and veriserve , a prototype verifiable LLM serving engine with PD disaggregation built around a formally verified KV-page lifecycle design model. Applying vstack to production Prefill-Decode serving uncovered three classes of real RDMA and cache concurrency bugs across SGLang and vLLM, resulting in 6 proposed upstream pull requests . Meanwhile, veriserve backs its PdLedger design model with a 226-module, 516,973-obligation TLAPS safety proof while adding only 0.18% mean p50 TPOT overhead on NVIDIA GB200. We believe verifiable serving defines the second half of LLM infra as autonomous coding agents write the deepest layers of production systems. Why is verifying an LLM serving engine so hard in the first place? Over the past three years, inference engines like vLLM and SGLang have evolved from single-node executors into asynchronous distributed systems, layering paged KV memory , shared prefix caching , and disaggregated prefill-decode RDMA transfers over the same pool of physical GPU KV pages. When a request times out or aborts, its cleanup now races across RDMA network cards, CPU cache trees, and GPU attention kernels simultaneously. Because GPUDirect RDMA writes directly into GPU memory without involving the target CPU, a lifecycle mismatch often does not crash the server, but returns HTTP 200 OK while silently mixing one user’s KV cache into another user’s response. aws-emulator

Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so.

It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog.

It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great if you could download a single binary and use that as part of a standard test suite in other languages and on other platforms.

title: How our GTM Agent builds consistent, high-quality sales artifacts
summary: Learn how LangChain built GTM Agent on Deep Agents to build high-quality, custom sales artifacts trained on business context.
story_key: story|title:how our gtm agent builds consistent high quality sales artifacts
content_excerpt: Over the last 12 weeks, our internal GTM Agent has saved LangChain's sales reps thousands of hours across its workflows. In that time, it generated 1,540 sales artifacts, which reps used to build by hand, one account at a time. These artifacts include customized account plans, proof-of-value documents, proposal decks, and onboarding plans. A powerful model can speed up artifact creation, one of the biggest time sinks in any deal, but can only take automation so far. What makes the biggest difference is everything built around the model: This post walks through how we used business context to build artifact generation with our GTM agent, and how we shaped it to fit the way LangChain sells. You can replicate this work on top of the Deep Agents harness. The primitives it depends on (a sandbox, skills, memory, and scheduled runs) are available in our managed version, Managed Deep Agents , so a team building something similar can get straight to capturing how its business runs. Earlier this year we wrote about how we built LangChain’s GTM Agent , which now runs a wide range of our sales and marketing workflows. It researches new leads and drafts personalized outreach for reps to approve in Slack, and every week it surfaces account signals like expansion opportunities and deal risks. Since reps were already using it every day, it was the natural place to take on one of the most time-consuming parts of their job: building sales collateral. That work was overdue for a fix. Inconsistent versions of the same document were showing up across the org. Account executives built proposal decks by pulling usage data into a chat assistant and assembling the deck themselves. The same work got repeated on every deal, and it looked different every time. We needed a way to standardize our hard-won lessons on what works without slowing anyone down. The third goal was the hardest to get right. Every stage of a deal has gates, or things that must happen before the deal can move forward, like naming an economic buyer or agreeing on success criteria. We track which stage every deal is in and which artifact helps clear each gate. But when this work was all manual, a skipped step usually came to light in a pipeline review, weeks after the rep could have asked the customer. Now that artifacts are filed through the GTM Agent, it can spot a missing one while the deal is still active. This workflow also gives our sales leaders a natural place to weigh in. title: Token Pooling-Aware Training for Multi-Vector Embedding Models
story_key: story|variant:embedding|title:token pooling aware training for multi vector embedding models
content_excerpt: Multi-vector embedding models give each query token its own opportunity to find a match in a document. This makes them wonderfully expressive for search, but those document vectors add up quickly. A corpus with millions of documents can contain hundreds of millions of vectors! Token pooling makes these representations smaller by merging similar token vectors. The more aggressively I compress them, however, the easier it becomes to lose something useful. Pooling-aware training teaches the encoder to preserve the information that matters when its vectors are merged, helping you retrieve better from the same storage budget. In this post, I'll explain how pooling works, train a model for compressed retrieval with Sentence Transformers, and explore the resulting quality and storage tradeoff. With pool_factor=4 , my normally trained model retains 94.6% of its unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10, with a 4x reduction in document vectors. Token pooling-aware training raises that retention to 97.8% at the same storage budget! Let's see how. This post builds on pooling-aware training studied in Stefan Josef's Learn to Pool and LightOn's pooling regularization study , which also explores targeted training and adaptive budgets. Here, I'll focus on understanding the method and putting it to work with a short, reproducible Sentence Transformers example. Pooling-aware training improves retrieval quality at the same vector budget. Details below. A single-vector embedding model compresses an entire document into one vector. Multi-vector models such as ColBERT instead keep a collection of contextual token vectors, allowing different parts of a query to match different parts of a document. For example, a query about a laptop with a long battery life can find evidence about the laptop in one part of a document and battery endurance in another. With MaxSim scoring, each query vector selects its best matching document vector, and those scores are added together: Even with the 2-bit or 4-bit residual quantization supported by Fast-PLAID , storing hundreds of vectors per document adds up. At 4 bits per residual coordinate, 200 vectors of 128 dimensions require 12.8 KB of quantized residuals per document, or 12.8 GB across a million documents. Pooling each document to 50 vectors reduces that to 3.2 GB, at the same dimensionality and precision. The useful observation is that many document vectors can be similar. title: Chain of Physics: Supporting Fault Diagnosis with Engineering-Inspired Large Language Model Reasoning
summary: Fault diagnosis in complex systems requires linking observed changes in physical quantities to the failure mechanisms that produce them. Experienced engineers perform this task by combining sensor information with knowledge of system behavior and fault propagation. Large Language Models (LLMs) can support this process, but their diagnostic reasoning depends on the availability of asset-specific engineering knowledge and on how this knowledge is represented and used during inference. This work introduces Chain of Physics (CoP), an LLM-based fault-diagnosis framework built around a Constrained Knowledge Graph (CKG) generated automatically from asset-specific reference documentation. CoP addresses failure-sensor association from textual engineering knowledge. The CKG stores diagnostic chains connecting failure modes, changes in physical quantities, and monitoring sensors. During inference, semantically similar graph paths are retrieved for each question and used as both information and in-context examples for the reasoning process. Candidate failure modes are extracted from the question and analysed independently through dedicated LLM calls, which generate plausible failure-to-observation chains. A final decision module compares these chains with the available answer choices. CoP is evaluated on the FailureSensorIQ benchmark across four industrial asset classes and three LLMs. Compared with direct prompting and conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), CoP improves diagnostic accuracy across all evaluated models, with gains ranging from 7.8 to 19.6 percentage points and from 11.7 to 18.2 percentage points, respectively. The results show that structured engineering knowledge can improve LLM-based diagnostic reasoning when graph retrieval is combined with in-context examples of fault propagation.

title: The Unused Input: The Initial State as a Conditioning Interface for Recurrent TSFMs
summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast unseen series without task-specific training. Increasingly they are built on recurrent backbones, whose constant per-step cost makes long-context inference cheap, and which, unlike transformers, carry a state. A recurrent backbone computes its prediction from two inputs: the observed context window and the initial recurrent state. In practice only the first is utilised and the initial state is unused by convention. We ask whether the initial state can be utilised in recurrent TSFMs. Using the xLSTM-based zero-shot forecaster TiRex as a case study, we freeze the backbone and train only a small head that writes a context vector into the initial state, so that any change in accuracy is attributable to the injected state rather than to adapted weights. A spectral summary of the input window, learned once and applied unchanged to every series, lowers mean GiftEval MASE by 0.175%, with every seed improving, which neither a parameter-matched LoRA adapter nor a learnable static state reproduces. An embedding of text attached to each series, evaluated on six MoTime datasets, reveals two roles for the state. As a per-dataset adaptation surface, a static state lowers MASE by 0.04-6.96% of the zero-shot baseline (8-70% of the gain of full fine-tuning). As a channel for exogenous information, the text-conditioned state lowers it by a further 0.15-0.41% of the zero-shot baseline on four of six datasets and, combined with a LoRA adapter, exceeds full fine-tuning, which has no access to the text, on one of them. In TiRex, the effect concentrates in the mLSTM blocks and is strongest at short context. The results are preliminary and the improvements small, but they point to the initial state as a direction for further research.

But more data doesn't automatically mean better insights. Inevitably, it means more places for an agent to look and more chances to find the wrong answer. Ask a frontier agent a question about your business and it starts a live search. It hops between MCP servers, opens a document, reads a schema, tries a table, backs out and tries another. It has little context on where the right answer lives, so it may guess its way through a random walk across the organization's data. What agents need is a map of the business before they start looking. That's why we announced Genie Ontology , the enterprise context layer, that combines governed definitions with continuously learned organizational knowledge giving AI agents the business understanding they need to deliver trusted insights. Today we are introducing new Databricks Genie plugins that give your team’s favorite agents a governed interface to access your enterprise context. These plugins work natively today in ChatGPT , Claude , Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Grok Bot so teams can maintain business context in Databricks and make it available across their preferred agents. Frontier agents can now draw on Genie Ontology to supply the definitions, relationships, and source context needed to interpret the business. Genie works out what the business terms mean, finds the right data across tables and documents, writes and runs SQL and returns an answer with citations to its sources. For questions requiring specialized analysis, Genie can route work to domain-specific Genie Agents . A question about pipeline attribution routes to the marketing Genie Agent. title: Earlybird: Predictive Streaming Speech Recognition in 29M Parameters
summary: Streaming speech recognizers output a word only after the speaker has finished it, typically 90-400 ms later. For a voice agent every millisecond counts: the sooner the words are outputted, the sooner the agent can start a search or plan its reply. We present Earlybird, a 29M-parameter streaming recognizer (16.8 MB at 4 bits). Earlybird learns from audio cut off at random points, including partway through a word, and is asked to predict every word that is due by then in full, plus a guess of the next two words. Its raw token probabilities give a confidence for every word including the one still being spoken. On clean audiobook speech (LibriSpeech test-clean), the median word is predicted correctly 90 ms before the speaker finishes it, while released streaming models get it 90 to 400 ms after it ends. Earlybird is the earliest on all six test sets we time, covering audiobooks, TED talks, public speech, earnings calls, and synthetic speech. On the same audiobooks, 69% of words are predicted correctly before they end, against 3-25% for the other models. For words still being spoken, confidence is calibrated, with an expected calibration error (ECE) of 3.7 to 5.5. On the eight English Open ASR Leaderboard sets, it is more accurate than Moonshine Tiny on every set and roughly ties Whistle, a model of the same size.

title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
summary: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget. On Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B with simulated round-to-nearest weight quantization (8, 6, 4 and 3 bits, fp16 reference), read from the logits of the letters A to D on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU and HellaSwag (300 items each), 6 bits lose no accuracy against fp16 (they score +1.8 (+1.0 to +2.5) and +0.9 (+0.3 to +1.5) points higher, which we do not explain), and 8 bits change it by -0.7 (-1.1 to -0.3) and -0.4 (-0.7 to -0.2) points. At 4 bits the answer-slot skew rises from 0.15 to 0.53 (0.6B) and from 0.07 to 0.12 (1.7B); Gaussian noise at the same weight SNR gives 0.15 and 0.37 (two draws) and 0.19 (one draw), so the control is inconclusive on whether rounding adds slot skew beyond equal-power noise. Flip rates rise but stay below an accuracy-matched baseline of independent uniform errors. Averaging four cyclic orders recovers +12.6 points at 4 bits for 0.6B (+5.3 at fp16). We price bits and passes in one machine-independent unit, weight bytes read times passes. In cost-matched pairs, extra orders beat extra bits only when the weights have 6 or more bits, and the decision table reduces to: use 6-bit weights and spend the rest of the budget on up to four orders, one pass each. Everything is simulated on two small models with the simplest quantizer; a title-level search found no earlier study of quantization together with option order.

Handshake went from launch to $1B in one year pushing the envelope of specialized data for frontier labs. Our first deep dive into a data lab with specific examples across Finance, Bio, and Alignment This is our first Latent Space deep dive with an AI data company . In roughly a year, Handshake’s AI training business went from launch to $1 billion in gross annualized revenue . What are frontier labs buying at that scale? What evals are models still nowhere close to human level on? Garrett Lord brought the people who build these reinforcement learning environments to show us. For the first time, we are walking through them live! To cover the scope of Handshake, we had to produce a very special joint podcast across our Science/Engineering/Research/Finance podcast hosts, because Handshake’s business runs across all these and more. Finance. In the finance demo, the agent has to find its assignment in a bank’s email, work out which files govern the deal, and deliver a workbook. Watch what happens to one line in the client’s email about existing goodwill. The agent carries the number into Python and subtracts it. Collin points out that the model can explain the tax treatment when you ask it directly. The mistake comes when it has to recognize that this particular line of code is where the rule applies. Bio. Nick Magazine and Jonas Mueller show us VIALS, Handshake’s benchmark for interpreting the images scientists use at work. Nick puts nine slides of brain-tumor tissue on screen and asks which two show the most advanced vessel necrosis. Give yourself a moment before his answer. Nick picks H and I. The model picks those two and adds G. Watching Nick point to what’s missing from the tissue is more instructive than seeing the score. Coding. In a simulated file-access task, the team can inspect which files an agent read, whether it checked the copies, and what it did to the shell history afterward. A transcript of the agent’s final reply would miss most of what Steve Kelling and Nishant Ranka are evaluating. 🟣 AI data business — Garrett Lord, Sahil Bhaiwala and Nishant Ranka open and close the episode on the market for expert data. 🌸 Life scien

title: claude-code v2.1.319
summary:
What's changed

  • Changed auto mode with telemetry or feature flags off, including behind LLM gateways: calls the server can't check are asked about or denied, with no fallback to the built-in classifier; set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 to keep using it (Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry are unchanged)
  • Changed auto mode behind an LLM gateway: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=1 turns on the server-side check even with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS set; if managed settings set the latter, they must set the 1 too
  • Added support for MCP tasks in the terminal: when an MCP server runs a tool call as a task, Claude Code moves it to the background right away and tells Claude the result when it finishes
  • Added the CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND environment variable to make Claude Code wait for an MCP task inside its tool call instead of moving it to the background right away
  • Added permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting setting: a tool call that would wait on a permission prompt is denied and the turn continues, in terminal sessions, subagents and teammates
  • Added /claude-api latency-optimize to find where your Claude API code makes people wait and try faster settings against your eval
  • Added the CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEATURE_FLAGS environment variable, which stops feature-flag fetching without turning off telemetry; every flag then uses its built-in default
  • Added spend for today, this week and this month to /usage for developers behind a Claude apps gateway who have no spend limit, when the gateway runs this version or later
  • Added admin.pooled_conflict_rule and admin.pooled_priority_order to the Claude apps gateway, to set which pooled group budget pays first for a developer in several groups
  • Added an optional login_notice setting to the Claude apps gateway that shows an operator-defined message on the gateway's browser verification page and on Claude Code's sign-in screen
  • Added CLAUDE_GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT=json to the Claude apps gateway: operational log lines become JSON with severity, time and message, for log collectors that read the level from a field
  • Added a Claude apps gateway boot warning for a case where another policy's availableModels also allows a custom model id that one policy lists by name
  • Added start-up warnings to the Claude apps gateway for policies with no desktopHome that rely on coworkTabEnabled: false or chatSessionRetentionDays, ahead of Claude Desktop's November 10 change
  • Added a warning when your claude.ai login ends and Claude Code continues on the sign-in from ant auth login, which bills usage to your Claude Console organization
  • Added a line at startup naming the Claude Console organization that is billed in a case where Claude Code uses the sign-in from ant auth login
  • Added an "Earlier in this session" row to /tasks that lists finished subagents, so you can reopen one and message it even after it leaves the list or you restart
  • Added a note to /loop confirmations in cloud sessions that a timer stops with its container, with an offer of a loop that survives
  • Fixed MCP servers on the older handshake failing to connect, or returning empty results, because Claude Code declared an extension that it only uses with newer servers
  • Fixed a long-running MCP tool call on a claude.ai connector sometimes never reporting its result after --resume
  • Fixed a session's diff failing to load on claude.ai and the mobile apps when the folder Claude Code runs in has a file or folder named HEAD
  • Fixed /diff showing "Diff unavailable" when a git repository has a file or folder named HEAD at its top level
  • Fixed the /diff pane opening blank in sessions where 64 or more turns edited files
  • Fixed slash commands typed after a leading space, tab or newline being sent to Claude as plain text instead of running
  • Fixed a request that kept failing with a 401 refreshing your login on every retry and causing 401s in your other sessions
  • Fixed /context sending its full visual grid to Claude on every later turn; Claude now reads only the table
  • Fixed claude -p exiting 0 in auto mode when its actions were refused because no safety check was available: text and JSON output now exit 1
  • Fixed a case where Claude Code listed every project file at start on Linux for projects on a network file system (NFS, SMB, Lustre and similar)
  • Fixed a case where auto mode was wrongly refused when a client sent a model change and a request for auto mode back to back
  • Fixed /status showing "Auto mode server: Enabled" when the server-side review isn't reaching the session, for example behind an LLM gateway that drops it
  • Fixed Claude-drafted feedback, surveys and /feedback continuing to appear after the server refused feedback for your organization
  • Fixed Claude drafting feedback on third-party gateways, where it can't be sent
  • Fixed auto mode refusing actions without saying why when permission rules or autoMode settings are very large: it now explains and, unless autoMode deny rules are set, asks you in the terminal
  • Fixed a case where Bash deny and ask rules missed commands written with quoted words
  • Fixed subagent hand-back reports showing an internal marker and provenance note when expanded outside verbose mode
  • Fixed claude -p --resume with a prompt losing a deferred tool call when its MCP server is missing: the run now exits 1, keeps the call and refuses later input
  • Fixed a case where text was dropped from informational messages sent to SDK clients
  • Fixed a case where Agent SDK hosts got a generic exit-code error instead of a failed run's own error message when the disk was full
  • Fixed CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN re-running a turn that was interrupted in plan mode when the session resumes in another permission mode
  • Fixed edits to a settings file being ignored when made within a few seconds of Claude Code writing that file
  • Fixed a config file left at the legacy name hiding your setup with no warning: Claude Code now says on stderr when a home holds two config files, and which is in use
  • Fixed ~/.claude.json, settings and edited files ending up empty or cut off when the disk fills during a save in a read-only folder or to a bind-mounted file (one session saving at a time)
  • Fixed Write ending the turn as a refusal when it couldn't read the file to overwrite
  • Fixed background Bash commands that finish almost instantly losing their output while being reported as completed
  • Fixed the Bash tool's diff of changed files missing a file that the command wrote just before it ended
  • Fixed a mistyped model name, such as opus-5-5, telling you to update Claude Code instead of suggesting the model you meant
  • Fixed a case where NotebookEdit changed the wrong cell when the notebook changed while a permission prompt was open
  • Fixed a ~0.5s hang after pressing Enter on the /login success screen: the dialog now dismisses immediately and the post-login refresh runs in the background
  • Fixed Ctrl+G not opening the external editor while typing an "Other" answer to a question in screen reader mode
  • Fixed Monitor's WebSocket watch failing with "could not resolve" behind a proxy when CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_RESOLVES_HOSTS is set and the machine has no DNS of its own
  • Fixed claude plugin eval warnings suggesting max: 0 for a tool that must not be called, which could never pass
  • Fixed background plugin auto-update not installing a dependency added by the updated plugin version
  • Fixed Cmd+click not opening links in Ghostty over tmux in sessions opened from the agents view
  • Fixed a mod's hot reload in .claude/skills missing a file that was deleted just after it appeared, and missing its return
  • Fixed /rewind failing with "No files were restored" when restoring code to a checkpoint from before /branch
  • Fixed the /claude-api skill saying Console web settings don't apply to Managed Agents sessions, and tightened its credential and permission examples
  • Fixed needless permission prompts for read-only commands wrapped in a plain timeout DURATION, such as timeout 30 rg foo
  • Fixed WebFetch describing claude.ai shared-chat links as empty pages; it now says shared chats can't be read and to paste the conversation instead
  • Fixed Artifact database calls being re-sent to artifacts without a database; errors now say whether republishing helps
  • Fixed a case where artifact database reads that save to a folder (out_dir) were refused
  • Fixed detailed beta tracing not presenting CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT to collectors that require a client certificate
  • Fixed the OpenTelemetry claude_code.session.count metric counting Agent SDK prewarm() processes that were never claimed; a pre-started process now counts once, when it is claimed
  • Fixed /clear killing running commands of background agents, teammates and workflows that keep running, and foreground subagents of background agents and teammates
  • Fixed a terminal whose Claude apps gateway sign-in had expired sending telemetry and managed-settings requests that the gateway refused and logged as invalid_token
  • Fixed the agents view appearing to send a reply to a background session waiting on a permission prompt; the reply now stays in the box with a hint to open the session and answer
  • Fixed agent view removing a draft saved by another agent view in the same directory when exiting
  • Fixed a case where agent view came back with another agent view's input text after restarting itself for an update
  • Fixed the agents view preview cutting off long commands, results and status lines without an ellipsis, and dropping **, backticks and tags from commands waiting for approval
  • Fixed Claude in Chrome reporting the extension as not connected when the connection dropped mid-action; Claude now checks the page before repeating an action that may have run
  • Fixed Remote Control sessions still showing "Limit reached" on other devices after a usage limit was lifted outside the session
  • Fixed the file card sometimes missing in the Claude iOS app when Claude sent a single file
  • Fixed self-hosted runner sessions failing with no explanation when the server keeps refusing to renew model access: the runner now retries sooner and posts a warning in the session
  • Fixed /permissions in cloud sessions replying only that it isn't available; it now says where the session's rules live and how to change them
  • Fixed cloud sessions losing session-scoped deny and ask permission rules, such as those a PermissionRequest hook adds, when the session moves to a new worker
  • Fixed mod hot-reloading turning off for the session when you typed three messages instead of answering its question in a cloud session
  • Fixed background tasks that keep running after /clear disappearing from the task list in Claude Code on the web until another task started or ended
  • Fixed hidden commands appearing in the slash command menu of cloud sessions on mobile and web
  • Fixed a case where /rewind could restore or delete a file through a directory symlink
  • Fixed a case where a sed command could skip the permission check in accept-edits and auto mode
  • Fixed a case where CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=1 in managed settings was ignored behind an LLM gateway when the gateway's URL is set only there and server-managed settings can't be fetched
  • Fixed a Bash permission bypass where a crafted environment prefix could hide part of a command from permission checks
  • Fixed a case where deny and ask rules, hook matchers and disallowedTools entries written with a claude.ai connector's terminal name (mcp__claude_ai_Slack) were ignored in Claude Desktop (takes effect once Claude Desktop includes this version)
  • Fixed a sandbox escape when creating a worktree
  • Fixed self-hosted runners: --trust-workspace false now also stops hooks in the repository's settings files and skills from running
  • Fixed a case where idle background sessions started through a shell-exported LLM gateway left the gateway after an update
  • Fixed help links in /status and the auto mode billing notice opening only part of the address when they wrap
  • Fixed a case where certificate errors behind a TLS-inspecting proxy persisted when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC was set. With it set, Claude Code now makes a TLS handshake with the configured API host after a certificate failure, through your http:// proxy if one is set; it sends no API request
  • Fixed claude remote-control exiting silently with status 0 when a first-run question gets no answer (scripts, services, batch jobs, Ctrl+C); it now says why and exits 1
  • Fixed claude remote-control ignoring a piped y that has no newline after it at the first-run question; it now counts as a yes
  • Fixed /rename reporting plain success when the new name could not be saved to the session transcript; it now warns that the new name may not last
  • Fixed ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} not being substituted in a plugin-provided subagentStatusLine command, which can now reference the plugin's own scripts
  • Fixed claude plugin update and /plugin "Update now" not installing dependencies added by the new plugin version
  • Fixed subagents being told after compaction to expect a completion notice for background agents they neither started nor took over
  • Fixed a case where a background agent's later report was lost silently: the notification now says it was refused and how to ask for it
  • Improved config saves on Windows: Claude Code waits longer for a file another program has open, so a kill during a save is less likely to leave ~/.claude.json empty
  • Improved Claude in Chrome after a brief disconnect: it waits up to 6 seconds for the session's own browser to return before picking another
  • Improved Claude in Chrome: javascript_tool results of up to 60,000 characters now stay in the conversation instead of being saved to a file
  • Improved claude purge and the clean-up of old sessions to retry a folder that could not be fully deleted, and to report it as an error if it remains
  • Improved the refusal for a path outside the working directories on macOS and Windows: when only its letter case differs from a path inside them, the message names that spelling
  • Improved the contrast of faint gray secondary text, such as hints, details in /stats, /model and /sandbox, and rejected-action messages
  • Improved the artifact database error when an update targets a document that does not exist, and when the service pauses repeated refused writes
  • Improved the Claude apps gateway's warnings about a failed upstream call: each now names the upstream, not only its provider
  • Improved the Claude apps gateway's spend limit error: it reads "spend limit reached · resets Dec 1", then admin.blocked_message if one is set
  • Improved the /model picker: older models are now grouped under a "More models" row instead of being listed after the current ones
  • Improved /context at the terminal so the table Claude reads stays short: each list keeps its 10 largest rows, and MCP tools that load on demand share one row per server until they're called
  • Improved /usage in cloud sessions: it now links to Settings → Usage on claude.ai in a case where plan limits can't be shown
  • [VSCode] Improved the confirmation for removing a plugin marketplace: it now checks which of its plugins are installed at that moment
  • Changed MCP tasks to work in the terminal without feature-flag fetching (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, LLM gateways, DISABLE_TELEMETRY); set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASKS=1 to turn them off
  • Changed auto mode so that a project's settings files or a plugin can no longer switch its server-side check back on once you have switched it off outside the project
  • Changed Monitor's WebSocket watch to follow a rule on every Bash command: a deny refuses it, and under an ask rule an allow on Monitor, bypass mode or auto mode no longer skips the prompt
  • Changed CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_RESOLVES_HOSTS so that settings files can no longer set it where the host manages the network; set it in the process environment
  • Changed a session's exact Bash or PowerShell ask rule to be refused, not asked about, when a broader deny rule covers the command
  • Changed the Bash tool to ask for permission before running which with flags outside a lookup/display set
  • Changed --add-dir directories to register plugin marketplaces only once that directory's own trust dialog has been accepted
  • Changed nested skill loading: with the Bash sandbox on, skills in .claude/skills folders below the starting folder load only if you start Claude Code there or /cd there
  • Changed self-paced /loop to end when a turn finishes without rescheduling, instead of scheduling a fallback wakeup; set CLAUDE_CODE_LOOP_KEEPALIVE=1 to keep the old behavior
  • Changed PostToolUse hooks to run, with up to 10 seconds to finish, on tool calls that finish after a new message interrupts the turn
  • Changed what Claude is told after safeguards stop a subagent: retry with a narrower prompt or tell you, instead of doing the work itself
  • Changed cloud sessions to drop session-scoped allow rules at a move to a new worker when their deny and ask rules can't all be kept, so you may be asked again
  • Changed the automatic certificate repair behind a TLS-inspecting proxy: it no longer runs when ALL_PROXY is the only proxy variable set. Set HTTPS_PROXY to the proxy's http:// URL instead
  • Changed artifact database saves of rows others may have written: each file gets a hidden marker file, and existing files without one, earlier versions' exports among them, are left alone and reported
  • Updated /claude-api managed-agents-onboard templates to match the Claude Console: removed Performance tuner, renamed two, and turned off web search and fetch in five whose prompts don't use them
  • Removed shortcuts_list and shortcuts_execute, which listed and started shortcuts saved in the extension, from Claude Code's built-in Claude in Chrome tools
  • Gateway: Added startup warnings for upstreams that mix AWS GovCloud with other upstreams, and for base URL variables in the gateway's environment
  • Gateway: Added a start-up log warning when managed settings name an Amazon Bedrock guardrail in a header, which the gateway doesn't forward, and no bedrock upstream sets a guardrail
  • Gateway: Fixed Claude Desktop offering a web search tool that always failed when every upstream is Amazon Bedrock
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed a runner started with --use-anthropic-git-proxy or --configure-git registering before a failed startup check made it exit; it now exits first
  • Self-hosted runner: Changed CLAUDE_RUNNER_CHECKOUT_PATH so that each repository in a session gets its own folder: a folder name already taken in the session gets -2, -3, … at the end
  • Self-hosted runner: Removed the end-of-session upload of a session's debug log; a failed session's log stays on the runner host unless --remove-session-state is set
  • [VSCode] Fixed prompts over 50,000 characters being cut off silently: the prompt now stays in the chat box with a notice, and a paste over the limit is refused with a notice
  • [VSCode] Fixed a click on the survey or "Report a problem" buttons sending the unfinished prompt
  • [VSCode] Fixed cloud sessions opened from the extension's Web tab bringing back turns that /clear, or Retry or Edit of a typed prompt, had removed
  • [VSCode] Fixed a deleted session's file coming back when that session was renamed in the extension
  • [VSCode] Fixed Claude carrying out an unapproved plan after a window reload: a step interrupted in plan mode now stops with a notice when the session comes back in another permission mode
  • [VSCode] Improved the "not signed in" message behind a Claude apps gateway: it now looks like an error and has a Sign in link
  • [VSCode] Changed links in Claude's replies that point at Claude sign-in, connector or API addresses to show as text with the address, instead of opening in the browser
  • [VSCode] Fixed a possible chat panel freeze when a dropped item's path contains a very long run of "/" characters
  • [VSCode] Fixed the claude-vscode.toggleDictation command starting dictation in every open Claude view at once; it now acts only in the view you are using, and a second press stops it
  • [VSCode] Fixed the chat panel slowing down while a reply with many unclosed $$ math fences, each shorter than the last, streams in
  • [VSCode] Improved the chat panel's diagnostics tool for large workspaces: it leaves out files with no problems, returns compact JSON, and accepts an optional minimum severity
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed scheduled tasks silently dropping a connector named memory: runs now keep it, mounted under that name plus a short suffix
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed Send now on a waiting message in cloud sessions ending running background agents; they now keep running
  • [Cloud sessions] Improved the stalled-setup warning on self-hosted environments: its link now prefers your organization's default or an environment with a live runner, and names it
  • [Code Review] Changed unlinking a GitHub organization to also turn off its All repositories setting in Code Review; it stays off after you relink until you turn it back on
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag setup blocking launch when the channel list couldn't fully load; admins can now launch without picking a channel
  • [Claude Tag] Added a Claude Tag row to the Models admin page for Enterprise orgs with Claude Tag connected, linking to where its model defaults are managed
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed saving auto mode allow rules in Claude Tag admin settings overwriting another admin's changes; the save is now refused with a message
